input: Plan a multi-generational holiday for the whole family

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of generations, total headcount, and age range (e.g. toddlers, teenagers, elderly grandparents) completely changes which destinations, activities, and accommodation setups are feasible.
The destination type (beach, city, countryside, abroad vs. domestic) defines the entire trip framework — transport, visas, climate, and activity options.
A shared family budget per person or overall cap determines accommodation tier, travel class, dining, and which activities are realistic.
Trip duration and travel window affect which destinations are reachable and how much can be packed in, especially around school holidays or work schedules.
Knowing whether the family wants a single shared property (e.g. villa) vs. a hotel with separate rooms vs. a resort changes the entire booking and coordination approach.
Understanding the priority balance between relaxation, sightseeing, and shared activities helps resolve conflicts between what different generations enjoy most.
Identifying what a 'successful' holiday looks like — e.g. everyone gets quality time together, kids are entertained, older members are comfortable — clarifies which trade-offs to make when planning.

gold.taskDescription: Organise a holiday that brings together family members across multiple generations, accounting for everyone's needs, preferences, and practicalities.

questions.title: How many people are coming, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Establish the total headcount and the generational spread — for example, grandparents, parents, teenagers, and young children — as this is the single biggest driver of destination and activity suitability.

questions.title: What type of destination are you imagining?
questions.description: Determine whether the family is drawn to a beach resort, countryside retreat, city break, theme-park holiday, or somewhere else entirely, and whether travelling abroad or staying domestic is preferred.

questions.title: What is the total or per-person budget for this trip?
questions.description: Capture the financial envelope — whether it is a tight shared budget, a mid-range spend, or open-ended — so accommodation, flights, and activities can be planned accordingly.

questions.title: When are you planning to travel, and for how long?
questions.description: Pin down the travel window (specific dates or a rough season) and the intended trip length, taking into account school holidays, work leave, and any fixed commitments across generations.

questions.title: Do you want one shared property or separate hotel rooms?
questions.description: Clarify whether the group wants to stay together under one roof (e.g. a rented villa or holiday cottage) or prefers individual rooms in a hotel or resort, as this shapes the entire booking strategy.

questions.title: What should the holiday feel like day-to-day?
questions.description: Understand the preferred balance between relaxing downtime, group sightseeing or excursions, and activities that split by age group — and whether a structured itinerary or a loose, flexible pace is wanted.

questions.title: What would make this holiday feel like a real success?
questions.description: Identify the one or two outcomes the family cares about most — such as genuine togetherness, keeping every generation comfortable, creating a memorable milestone, or minimising stress for the organiser.
